abstract: MASLD and obesity characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation are known risk factors to manifest into Type 2 diabetes (T2D). Increased hepatic lipids due to interorgan cross talk leads de novo lipid synthesis which induce insulin resistance in multiple organs resulting in hyperglycemia. We evaluated two known lipid reducing Ayurvedic formulations, Arogyavardhini Rasa (AVR) and Nishamalaki Rasayana (NA), to understand their mechanistic basis. Network medicine-based analyses identified 128 phytochemicals in AVR and 182 in NA that met the predefined filtering criteria. The reported targets of both formulations showed significant network proximity to genes associated with T2D, fatty liver disease and obesity. An integrated knowledge graph linking formulations, phytochemicals, protein targets, FDA-approved drugs and disease genes enabling systems-level exploration of these relationships revealed eight targets, namely PPARA, PPARG, AKT1, SIRT1, TNF, PPARD, SERPINE1, and ACE which were common to both drugs. In the animal study, both formulations reduced high-fat-diet-associated increases in blood glucose, cholesterol, liver enzymes, macrovesicular and microvesicular hepatic steatosis. Untargeted liver metabolomics showed AVR and NA treatment restored sugar and nucleotide, pentose phosphate, bile and lipid metabolism pathways that were perturbed in response to high fat diet. Taken together, AVR and NA restored hepatic lipid homeostasis and inhibited manifestation of T2D.
